record.original_question: For the EKG sequence defined by a_1=1, a_2=2, and for n≥3 taking a_n to be the smallest unused positive integer with gcd(a_n,a_{n-1})≥2, determine the asymptotic structure of the associated 4-regular graphs. In particular, decide whether the observed cone/parabola-type geometry persists for large N and explain why the second eigenvalue stays suspiciously close to 4.

evidence.quote: The EKG sequence, first introduced by Jonathan Ayres (A064413, [12]), is a famously tricky sequence. Its definition is simple: a_1 = 1, a_2 = 2 and for each n ≥ 3, a_n is the smallest natural number that has not yet appeared with the property that gcd(a_n, a_{n-1}) ≥ 2.
Embedding the graph into R^3, we observe a type of parabola or cone structure. It is not clear to us what will happen as the graphs get larger and larger.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the EKG sequence $(a_n)_{n\ge 1}$ by $a_1 = 1$, $a_2 = 2$, and for every $n \ge 3$, $a_n$ is the smallest positive integer not already appearing among $a_1,\dots,a_{n-1}$ such that $\gcd(a_n, a_{n-1}) \ge 2$. (It is known that this sequence is a permutation of the positive integers.)

For each integer $N \ge 1$, construct a graph $G_N$ as follows. The vertex set is $\{1, 2, \dots, N\}$. Draw an edge between distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ whenever
$$\gcd(a_i, a_j) \ge 2 \quad\text{and}\quad |i - j| \le 2,$$
or, more generally, define $G_N$ to be the natural $4$-regular graph (away from boundary vertices) associated with the EKG sequence in which each vertex $i$ is connected to the indices of the two nearest preceding and two nearest following terms sharing a nontrivial common factor with $a_i$. Embed $G_N$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ using a standard spectral embedding via the eigenvectors corresponding to the smallest nonzero eigenvalues of its (combinatorial) Laplacian.

Let $\lambda_1(G_N) = 4 \ge \lambda_2(G_N) \ge \cdots$ denote the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix of $G_N$.

(a) Determine the limiting geometric structure of the spectral embedding of $G_N$ as $N \to \infty$. In particular, prove or disprove that the embedded vertices asymptotically concentrate on a cone or paraboloid-type surface.

(b) Determine $\lim_{N\to\infty} \lambda_2(G_N)$, and explain rigorously why $\lambda_2(G_N)$ remains extremely close to $4$ for all large $N$ (i.e., bound the spectral gap $4 - \lambda_2(G_N)$ asymptotically).
artifact.category_tag: spectral graph theory of integer sequences
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any work resolving the asymptotic geometric or spectral structure of the 4-regular graphs associated with the EKG sequence (OEIS A064413). Known results on the EKG sequence (Lagarias–Rains–Sloane, 2002) concern the asymptotics of $a_n$ itself, not these graphs. No source establishes the cone/parabola embedding limit or pins down the second eigenvalue asymptotics, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A064413 - OEIS
status_evidence.snippet: The EKG sequence: a(1)=1, a(2)=2; thereafter a(n) is the smallest number not already used which shares a factor with a(n-1). Lagarias–Rains–Sloane conjectures concern asymptotics of a(n).
status_evidence.claim: Existing literature on A064413 addresses term-asymptotics, not spectral/graph-embedding behavior.

status_evidence.title: The limit points of the top and bottom eigenvalues of regular graphs
status_evidence.snippet: General results on second eigenvalues of regular graphs do not specialize to EKG-derived graphs.
status_evidence.claim: No specialized result for EKG graph spectra was found.
